dossier.architecture: Wood-framed turret scorer with floating acquisition and gyro-timed swinging traversal climb.

subsystems.drivetrain: SDS MK4i; most motors kept near floor for stability.
subsystems.intake: Floating broad collector with mecanum centering and grippy top/bottom rollers.
subsystems.transfer: Two-stage ball path and upper color sensing; rejection followed by a recovery/staging motion.
subsystems.scoring: Long-developed turret/flywheel family with added controlled backspin; close-goal fallback shots.
subsystems.endgame: Central lifting arm plus reaching arms uses measured robot angle and swing momentum rather than timers.
subsystems.controls: PathPlanner autonomous from extensively tuned swerve; vision owns teleop targeting after odometry drift.

versions: Intake bracing added after early competition. Camera-independent autonomous and fixed close-range shots provide fallback capability.
dossier.analysis: A strong PCH example of familiar construction and retained design knowledge. The climb intentionally uses swing instead of eliminating it, so copying its hooks without the gyro-based sequence misses the essential behavior.
limits: Reported performance and prototype history are attributed to the source; not every intermediate revision is recoverable.

context_documents.title: 2022-1771 · Long-lived turret experience does not remove staging and rejection requirements
context_documents.body:
# 2022-1771: Long-lived turret experience does not remove staging and rejection requirements

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A floating broad collector and mecanum centering feed two-stage transport with color sensing and rejection recovery. The turret/launcher family has several historical iterations, including earlier-season examples, with controlled backspin in this version.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly describes iteration of a familiar turret family rather than a wholly new 2022 mechanism.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Existing know-how can reduce development risk, but the new game’s piece state, rejection legality and contact path still require testing. A rejected ball may disturb the next staged piece, so recovery is part of useful cycle time.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test rejection followed immediately by scoring and verify turret range/cable limits with the actual 2022 configuration.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/ZYonfJLN_q8](https://youtu.be/ZYonfJLN_q8)

source_reviews.title: Behind the Bumpers with North Gwinnett at Championship
source_reviews.locator: 1:37–4:24 intake and sorting; 4:28–6:12 launcher and fallback; 6:15–8:27 climb; 8:32–12:20 drive, controls and structure
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the full available English automatic caption track, including the start and end. Technical details are attributed to team speakers. No visual inspection claimed.
facts: The floating intake rides in a channel and uses grippy upper and lower rollers. The team added wood braces after early competition.
Upper-stage color detection changes the turret shot and cycles the next ball down and back to allow recovery.
Gyro angle gates a climb that deliberately uses swing momentum. The team describes low-mounted motors and inverted swerve.
source_reviews.limitations: Team performance estimates and material durability anecdotes are self-reports. The captions describe momentary inventory tactics without establishing a general legal capacity or rule interpretation.

source_reviews.title: North Gwinnett Robotics team site
source_reviews.limitations: Gallery wording alone establishes identity, with no inspection of internal geometry.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Robosaurus combined a tall launcher and swing climber with an effort to keep the motor mass low. Wood was used in the structure and gave the team a quick way to add braces. The shot system drew on several generations of turret experience, while the important Rapid React-specific work lay in staged ball flow, rejection and what to do after a loss of target.
piece_flow: The floating intake channels cargo inward with centering contacts and grippy rollers above and below.
Two transport stages separate storage from the upper color check.
The turret scores good cargo or changes angle, hood and speed for an unwanted one. The following ball can move down and return while the shooter recovers.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The team cites inverted MK4i modules for protection and reports concentrating motors within the bottom few inches. Keep the structural bracing outside the intake’s working float, and check the tall assembly against the climb swing. The team’s static height and its hangar swept volume are different design constraints.

subsystems.name: Floating collector and wood structure
subsystems.construction: Floating channel, upper and lower grippy contacts and added wood bracing joined with screws and glue.
subsystems.operation: Let the mechanism follow its channel while drawing cargo from across the front.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team chose the channel approach to avoid sending cargo over bumpers and added braces after early flex.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Wood makes local changes easy, but point loads and joint repeatability govern the stiffness that the next roller actually sees.
subsystems.interfaces: Brace position must preserve intake float and keep roller alignment with the lower stage.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Track deformation after offset hits, moisture exposure and several remove-and-reinstall cycles.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact wood species, panel thicknesses and structural load paths unresolved.

subsystems.name: Two-stage indexer and inherited turret
subsystems.construction: Lower staging, upper color sensor and a multi-generation hooded flywheel turret with backspin control.
subsystems.operation: Score or reject using different presets. Cycle the following cargo away and back while the shooter changes state.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team links repeated iteration to fast spin-up and cites close-goal fallback shots.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Measure reject-to-score recovery separately from launch rate. A quick change in commanded speed does not establish that the first subsequent good ball gets the intended release.
subsystems.interfaces: Index position and shot mode are coupled through the timing of the upper color reading.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test correct/wrong/correct arrivals and a camera disconnect during staging.
subsystems.unknowns: Sensor positions and verified speed recovery are unknown.

subsystems.name: Swing climber
subsystems.construction: Center arm initially lifts onto mid. Other arms support and reach while the robot tips.
subsystems.operation: Trigger the next motion from measured orientation and use the swing to reach the next bar.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team preferred angle feedback because impacts and swing can invalidate elapsed-time assumptions.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A gyro angle alone cannot distinguish opposite directions through the same angle. Check angular rate and support state in any transferred design.
subsystems.interfaces: Reach depends on loaded center of mass and hangar clearance.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test displaced starts, slow swings and bad readings before commanding transfer.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact angle thresholds and hook load distributions are unresolved.

subsystems.name: Swerve, auto and teleop aiming
subsystems.construction: Inverted MK4i modules, PathPlanner autonomous paths and camera lock for teleop.
subsystems.operation: Use short-duration odometry in auto, then have the operator orient the turret before vision takes over in teleop.
subsystems.team_rationale: Defense and wheel slip made long-duration dead reckoning drift too far for their shot aim.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A sensor can be adequate over a short horizon and inadequate over a whole match. Define the range of acceptable pose uncertainty for each operation.
subsystems.interfaces: Close-range fallback and camera-independent paths need their own calibrations.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Measure pose error after impact and reacquire from a deliberately wrong pose.
subsystems.unknowns: Claimed auto accuracy has no reviewed trial sample.

revisions: Added intake bracing. The 2022 turret added spin control to the inherited family.
transferable_principles: Build a specific recovery motion into the rejection sequence.
Gate swing-dependent transfers on measured state.
disconfirming_conditions: A flexible mounting material loses its repair advantage if repeated service moves alignment beyond the launch tolerance.
A swing-driven climb loses viability if it needs more free space or a narrower capture window than the field allows.
remaining_gaps: As-built joint construction, climber control logic, event-level cycle and reliability measurements.
recommended_images: Request a front image of the bracing and intake guides, a side cross-section of staging and turret entry, and a multi-pose climb view.
